job: Converting prospective fabless and hyperscaler evaluations into signed leading-edge foundry commitments for named AI accelerators on the advanced node.
outcome: A second external customer beyond Alphabet publicly commits a named AI part to the 18A or 14A node.
motivation: A merchant-fab franchise needs a proof-point customer roster, not a single in-house Alphabet job, to be credible.

task.what: Close evaluating designers into signed advanced-node tape-out agreements
task.where: Customer engagements and foundry contract negotiations
task.why: Establishes Intel Foundry as a credible second-source merchant fab
task.how: On-record customer announcement or signed foundry agreement

job: Bringing 18A yield, performance, and schedule to volume-ready maturity so prospective AI customers will commit leading-edge parts.
outcome: An 18A node hitting yield and schedule targets credible enough for an external customer to commit a named AI part.
motivation: The named counter-risk is 18A yield or schedule slipping, sending customers to TSMC for leading-edge volume.

task.what: Stabilize 18A defect density and ramp volume yield
task.why: De-risks the node so customers choose Intel over TSMC

job: Running the 18A process evaluation and porting a leading-edge AI accelerator or networking part toward tape-out on an Intel node.
outcome: A committed tape-out or on-record decision naming an AI part built on Intel's 18A or 14A node.
motivation: A credible second-source leading-edge foundry diversifies supply away from sole-source TSMC dependence for custom AI silicon.

task.what: Qualify PDK and port accelerator design to 18A
task.where: Customer design flow against Intel's 18A PDK
task.why: Diversifies leading-edge supply beyond sole-source TSMC
task.how: Intel 18A process design kit and tape-out flow
